title: Help educators share course materials with clear permission and attribution
description: Audience: bootcamp instructors and course directors sharing slides, readings, code and learner-created work through Zedu. Zedu’s public File Management page documents course-resource storage and sharing, but sharing capability does not establish permission to redistribute a resource. Produce one practical, plain-language course-material sharing kit: an ownership/permission/source/attribution register; a short pre-upload checklist; an instructor decision guide for own materials, third-party resources and learner-created work; and worked examples with clearly labelled fictional placeholders. Record what is verified, unknown or awaiting the rights holder’s answer. Check actual published licence terms and source links for any real example; do not give blanket legal assurances or invent a licence or permission. Done when another educator can use the kit to record a sharing decision and identify what must be confirmed before upload. Measure completeness using five synthetic examples with explicit pass/hold reasons, including missing permission and missing attribution. This is an educational workflow draft, not legal advice or a new privacy policy. Keep separate from platform role permissions, security/trust pages, file-findability tests, migration guides and marketing-content distribution. No real learner files, messages, uploads, permission changes, outreach or publication. Reuse existing onboarding and file guidance rather than commissioning another general product tutorial. One coherent kit; do not split it into small tasks for points.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: A one-page "Can I share this?" decision guide with ready-made attribution lines
acceptedWorkstreams.description: A plain-language flowchart for instructors before they upload: their own work; their institution's materials; third-party copyrighted content (slides, book scans, paid courses); openly licensed work (CC BY, CC BY-SA, CC BY-NC); and learner-created work, which needs the learner's consent. Each branch ends in a clear action: share, link instead, ask, or don't share. Includes copy-paste attribution lines for CC works, a naming convention for files in Zedu's File Management (title - author - licence), and a short "if you're unsure" note. It describes Zedu features only as the public File Management page does, and it's not legal advice. Done: the one-pager plus 5 worked examples.
